_about: The unit record: what every data/units/<id>.json carries. scripts/sim/unit_def.gd VALIDATES EACH FILE AGAINST THIS at load: a field listed here and missing from a file is a load error, never a default; a field in a file and not listed here is a load error too (it catches a misspelt key that would otherwise be ignored). Files starting with '_' are not units. The SHAPE is PROPOSED by Track S, 2026-10-09; the design doc's unit design sheet (Execution plan > Design work > Unit design sheets) lists what a full sheet holds, and the fields not here yet (specials, armor, shadow behaviour, card contents) come with the unit sheets; weapons were added by Track C, 2026-10-09.

conventions.units: Metres, seconds, metres per second, metres per second squared. Angles are DEGREES in data and radians at runtime (unit_def.gd converts).
conventions.frame: World x to the right, y DOWN (the prototype's canvas and Godot 2D). A heading of 0 points along +x; a positive turn is clockwise on screen (a right turn); the direction of motion is Vector2(cos(heading), sin(heading)).
conventions.value_record: Every tunable is a value record. While it is a placeholder: {"value": v, "_proposed": true, "_reason": "one line"}. Once a variant board or Alex sets it: {"value": v, "decision": "<id in data/decisions/decisions.json>"}. A record with neither is a load error, so no number can enter the game without saying where it came from (working rules 2 and 3). Plain fields (kind text or enum) are identity, not tuning, and are not records.
conventions.keys_starting_with_underscore: Comments. Allowed anywhere, ignored by the loader.

kinds.number: a value record holding a number >= 'min' (and <= 'max' where given)
kinds.integer: a value record holding a whole number >= 'min'
kinds.bool: a value record holding true or false
kinds.curve: a value record holding [[speed_mps, value], ...]: at least one point, speeds strictly increasing, values >= 0. Read by straight-line interpolation between points and held flat beyond the first and last point.
kinds.band_list: a value record holding a non-empty list of band ids from data/sim/altitude.json, no repeats
kinds.band: a value record holding one band id from data/sim/altitude.json
kinds.section: an object whose own fields are listed under 'fields'
kinds.points3: a value record holding a non-empty list of [forward, right, up] points, metres, in the airframe's axes (a weapon's hardpoints)
kinds.list: a plain list of objects, each validated against 'item_fields' (the weapons); the list is structure, the fields in each item are the tunables
kinds.material: a value record holding one material of the vocabulary in data/sim/rounds.json (metal, stone, wood, earth, water): what a round that lands on the thing hits
kinds.round: a value record holding one round id of data/sim/rounds.json: what a weapon fires

id.about: Unit type id; must equal the file name without .json. The World's units refer to it as their 'type'.

name.about: Display name, from the design doc's Initial unit roster.

domain.about: From the Initial unit roster table.

mobility.about: Track S2, 2026-10-10 (the strike). 'static' units never move, turn or plan: a radio tower, an anti-aircraft battery. The World refuses to plan them, gives them one step a turn that stands still, and does not wait for them in the ready-up; their envelope must be all zeros (unit_def.gd checks). 'mobile' is every unit that flies, drives or sails. Identity, not a number.

size_m.about: Largest planform dimension: wingspan for aircraft, length for tanks and ships. Drawing scale and, later, hit size.

draught_m.about: Track WS, 2026-10-10 (water): the depth of water a SEA unit needs under it. The World (World.set_water, data/sim/sea.json) keeps a sea unit's steps on water at least this deep, at its centre and at both ends of its hull; a step that would leave it is slowed or held (the "shore" limit). Greater than 0 for a unit of domain sea, exactly 0 for every other domain (unit_def.gd checks both). PROPOSED shape.

actions_per_turn.about: Steps per turn: the number of points on the unit's motion curve each turn. data/sim/turn.json splits turn_seconds into this many equal steps.

health.about: Hit points; the unit card's pips. Combat (scripts/sim/combat_resolver.gd) takes a weapon's damage_pips from it per hit; at 0 the unit is down.

sight_range_m.about: Vision radius for fog of war. Carried, unused until Track F's first vision rule reads it.

drawing.about: How the unit is drawn. Carried, unused by the simulation.

silhouette.about: Silhouette id for the drawing layer; chosen from a variant board (design doc, Unit design sheets).

material.about: WHAT THE UNIT IS MADE OF, for what a round does when it hits (builder G3, 2026-10-12; Alex, decisions damage-looks, 'the model makes sense', everything names a material, and gunfire-looks, G3: the materials told apart by lightness). One word of the ONE vocabulary of data/sim/rounds.json (metal, stone, wood, earth, water), the same words the line-of-fire grid's cells and a unit's shape boxes use. The effects feed looks the impact up by this and the round (data/fx/fx.json gunfire); a unit with parts of two materials (a battery's sandbag ring and its guns) names its main one here and each box its own. Every value is PROPOSED (the board's table, variants/gunfire/board.json material_table).

damage_smoke.about: WHAT THE UNIT SMOKES WITH once it is damaged (builder SMOKE, 2026-10-11; Alex, decisions smoke-consistency and impact-by-round-and-target: 'this should probably be a property of either the round or the thing being hit or both', puffs are not sized by the unit's length; the shape is PROPOSED). The effects layer (scripts/fx/fx_layer.gd) leaves a trail of puffs while 0 < health < full; this section is the THING THAT SMOKES: where on the unit the smoke comes from and how big that source is. The puffs are sized by the SOURCE (the engine deck, a funnel), never by the unit's size_m, so a 40 m bridge or a 120 m cruiser does not wear a puff as big as itself. Colour, life and growth stay in data/fx/fx.json (the damage smoke option); this is only the unit's part.

enabled.about: Whether this unit smokes when damaged at all. False for a thing that cannot (a stone bridge: Alex, 'Right now bridges don't have anything, that is fine.'): the effects feed leaves no smoke for it, with no special case in code.

source_m.about: The size of the smoke's source: a puff's radius is the option's radius_frac (W1: 0.34 at one pip lost, 0.8 at the last pip) times this. Proposed at 8 m at most (the lead's reading of Alex's 'a small source'); greater than 0 exactly when enabled (unit_def.gd checks).

source_back_m.about: Where the source is along the unit: metres BEHIND its centre on its heading (an engine deck at the rear of a tank, a funnel aft of amidships); negative is ahead of the centre, 0 is the centre.

rise_mps.about: How fast a puff climbs after it is born. A rising puff drifts with the wind at its height (data/sim/wind.json profile: faster higher up), so a plume stands over its source and leans downwind as it climbs, as the forest fire's does. Every unit that smokes shares the smoulder's rate of the wrecks and ruins (data/fx/fx.json crash and ruin smolder rise_mps; test_smoke_consistency holds them equal), a plane's trail and its fall trail too (Alex, decision smoke-consistency, 2026-10-12, asked whether planes' trails rise like ground smoke: 'Yes to both'); 0 only for a unit that does not smoke.

shape.about: THE UNIT'S BODY FOR LINES OF FIRE (builder LOF1, 2026-10-11, decision line-of-fire; PROPOSED shape and values). What a straight round can hit and what can stand in its way, as a few boxes (scripts/sim/line_of_fire_shapes.gd, scripts/sim/line_of_fire.gd). Alex: a ground vehicle is TWO boxes, hull and turret ('yes, two layers, hull and turret'); every other unit gets ONE box (the lead's proposal). Not read by combat yet (data/sim/line_of_fire.json enabled false). A box stands on its unit's BASE height: the ground under it (or the bridge's deck) for a surface unit, the water's surface for a boat, the band's absolute height for a plane (bands are absolute heights, data/sim/altitude.json), so a plane's box reaches below and above its band (bottom_m negative). Axes as the hardpoints': forward along the heading, right to its right (clockwise on screen).

boxes.about: The unit's boxes, the lowest layer first. A hull then a turret; a battery's sandbag ring then its guns. An empty list would mean a unit nothing can hit, which no unit is.

part.about: What the box is: 'hull', 'turret', 'body', 'deck', 'sandbags', 'guns'. A report names the visible share by part.

material.about: Its material, one word of the vocabulary of data/sim/rounds.json (metal, stone, wood, earth): what a round that stops on it would strike. Checked by unit_def.gd and test_line_of_fire. A STAMPED box of earth (a sandbag ring) puts the grid's raised-earth cell in the height grid.

kind.about: 'box': a rectangle length_m long and width_m wide. 'ring': an annulus, length_m its OUTER diameter and width_m its INNER diameter (a sandbag ring seen from above; a full ring, the art's gap is not modelled).

stamp.about: Whether this box is put into the height grid as an obstacle while the unit stands (a static unit's sandbag ring, a bridge's deck: other lines are blocked by it). A mobile unit's box is a target only, so false.

standable.about: Whether other units stand ON the stamped box (the bridge's deck: a tank on the bridge stands at the deck's top, not at the river's). Only meaningful with stamp true.

forward_m.about: The box centre's offset from the unit's centre, along its heading.

right_m.about: The box centre's offset to the unit's right.

length_m.about: Along the heading (a box), or the outer diameter (a ring).

width_m.about: Across it (a box), or the inner diameter (a ring).

bottom_m.about: The box's underside above the unit's base height. Negative for a plane, whose base is the band's height.

top_m.about: The box's top above the unit's base height.

envelope.about: The performance envelope (scripts/sim/envelope.gd). Each step the player picks a point; the envelope decides which points are reachable from the unit's state at the start of the step. Inertia: speed changes at most accel/decel per second, heading at most the turn rate at the step's starting speed, and turning and climbing cost speed.

speed_min_mps.about: Slowest the unit flies or moves. Aircraft: stall speed (a plane never falls below it from above it; no stall rule yet). Ground and sea: 0, or negative for the fastest reverse.

speed_cruise_mps.about: The unit's normal speed: where a new unit starts unless placed otherwise, and what the dumb AI flies at.

speed_max_mps.about: Top speed in level flight or on the level.

dive_speed_max_mps.about: Never-exceed speed: a dive may carry the unit past speed_max_mps up to this; above speed_max it then sheds speed at its full deceleration. Equal to speed_max_mps for units that cannot dive.

accel_mps2.about: Largest speed GAIN per second at full power. Per step it is accel x step_dt -- a rate, not a per-step figure, so a change to turn length or actions per turn does not silently change how hard a unit accelerates.

decel_mps2.about: Largest speed LOSS per second (throttle back, drag, brakes).

reverse_from_stop.about: Ships and tanks: true means speed cannot cross zero within a step; the unit must come to a stop, then may reverse (design doc, Motion and inertia: ships can reverse once stopped). Aircraft: false.

turn_rate_curve_dps.about: Largest heading change per second as a function of the speed at the start of the step (absolute speed when reversing). Planes: high at low speed, low at high speed (a tighter turn when slow). Ships: 0 at 0 speed, rising with way on (a rudder needs flow). Tanks: one flat point (pivot steering).

turn_bleed_mps2.about: Speed lost per second while turning at the full available rate, subtracted from both ends of the step's speed window. Planes lose speed in turns (design doc, Motion and inertia).

turn_bleed_exponent.about: Bleed for a partial turn is turn_bleed_mps2 x (turn used / turn available)^exponent. 2 tracks induced drag, which grows with the square of the load factor: gentle turns are nearly free, hard turns bite.

altitude_bands.about: The bands this unit may occupy, from data/sim/altitude.json. Aircraft: air bands. Ground and sea: ["surface"].

start_band.about: Band a new unit starts in unless placed otherwise; must be one of altitude_bands.

bands_per_step.about: Most bands the unit may climb or dive in one step. 0 for units that cannot change band.

climb_speed_cost_mps.about: Speed lost per band climbed in a step. A climb the unit cannot afford without falling below speed_min_mps is refused (the band stays).

dive_speed_gain_mps.about: Speed gained per band dived in a step; diving adds speed (design doc, Height). May carry the unit up to dive_speed_max_mps.

weapons.about: The unit's weapons, one record per CONE (Alex 2026-10-09: a bomber's tail turret and its front guns are different weapons). A gun sits on one or more HARDPOINTS (Alex): mount points on the airframe from which the cone starts, so a pair of wing guns is one weapon with two hardpoints, each rolling on its own. The model (geometry, odds, rolls, events) is documented in scripts/sim/combat.gd; the values are the lead's engagement-cones proposal (variants/engagement-cones/weapons_proposed.json) plus Track C's proposed odds and roll rate, all proposed, none Alex's yet. Angles are in the airframe's axes: 0 forward, 180 rearward, positive to the right and up. An empty list is a valid unit that cannot shoot.

id.about: The weapon's id, unique within the unit (combat events name it).

round.about: What the weapon fires (builder G3, 2026-10-12; Alex, decision round-model: a round per weapon; decision weapon-kinds: what a weapon fires decides its look): a round id of data/sim/rounds.json. The round carries the class, calibre, explosive, path, tracer and blast; the effects feed draws the muzzle smoke, the impact and the tracer from it (data/fx/fx.json gunfire, tracers).

kind.about: How it is mounted: fixed (points where the nose points), flexible (a gunner aims it within a cone) or turret (a powered mount with a wide arc). Identity, not a number: what it implies for the odds is in rim_odds_factor.

hardpoints.about: Where the cone starts: offsets from the unit's centre in the airframe's axes. One or more; each hardpoint rolls on its own, with its own cone.

mount_deg.about: The cone centre's direction relative to the nose, around: 0 forward, 180 rearward, positive to the right (clockwise seen from above).

half_across_deg.about: Half the cone's width: the most the target may be off the centre, sideways. 180 is ALL AROUND (Track S2, 2026-10-10: a flak battery fires at anything above it whichever way it faces): the azimuth is then not part of the cone test, only the height is.

elevation_deg.about: The cone centre's elevation above the airframe's level.

half_height_deg.about: Half the cone's height: the most the target may be off the centre, up or down. Firing between altitude bands is this same cone (Alex).

effective_range_m.about: The weapon's EFFECTIVE range, slant metres (3D, from the hardpoint): inside it the "range" odds factor is 1. Alex 2026-10-09: a gun fires slightly over its effective range, so past it the odds fall smoothly to 0 at effective_range_m x (1 + range_overshoot), range_overshoot being data/sim/combat.json's (one for every weapon). CombatWeapon.range_m is the same number under its old name.

base_hit_chance.about: The odds of one roll at the cone's centre, before any other factor.

rim_odds_factor.about: The 'centre' factor's value at the cone's rim: odds multiply by 1 at the centre falling to this at the rim. 1 is flat (flexible guns and turrets); well under 1 is peaked (fixed guns): a machine gun has better odds the nearer the target is to the centre of its cone (Alex).

falloff_exponent.about: The centre factor is 1 - (1 - rim_odds_factor) x r^falloff_exponent, r the normalized offset (0 centre, 1 rim). 1 falls in a straight line, 2 stays near the top longer. Unused when rim_odds_factor is 1.

tracking_dps.about: The "crossing_rate" odds factor (Alex 2026-10-10: relative velocity affects accuracy) is 1 / (1 + (rate / tracking_dps)^crossing_exponent), rate being the turn rate of the line of sight from the hardpoint to the target in degrees a second (the target's velocity relative to the shooter, across the line of fire, over the distance). So tracking_dps is the rate at which crossing halves the odds: small for a fixed gun (the pilot swings the whole plane), larger for a flexible gun or a turret (a gunner tracks). Closing speed costs nothing.

rolls_per_second.about: How often each hardpoint rolls while it has a target in the cone, on the turn's clock (data/sim/combat.json tick_seconds is the finest it can be resolved).

bomb_load.about: What the unit can drop (Track S2, 2026-10-10; Alex's decision bomb-load: several drops, i.e. several passes; the smaller the bomber, the fewer bombs, both per drop and in number of drops; everything gets at least two). A drop is a special taken in one step (scripts/sim/bombs.gd). Units that drop nothing carry 0 and 0. The bombs' physics (fall, cone, spread, blast) is shared and lives in data/sim/bombs.json.

drops.about: How many separate drops (passes) the unit can make. 0 for a unit that carries no bombs; otherwise at least 2 (Alex), which unit_def.gd checks.

per_drop.about: Bombs in one drop (a stick). 0 exactly when drops is 0.

specials.about: The unit's SPECIALS: what a step can switch on that is not a gun that fires on its own (Alex 2026-10-10: 'it should SAY in the step metadata the name of the special and the action. So Radio On, Bomb Drop, Turret Fire.'). One record per special; an empty list is a unit with none. PROPOSED shape (Track B, 2026-10-10; the words are Alex's): `id` is what the code calls it ('bomb' is the bomb drop of bomb_load, the plan request 'drop'; unit_def.gd checks a unit carries one exactly when it carries bombs), `name` is the thing ('Bomb', 'Radio') and `action` what is done with it ('Drop', 'On', 'Fire'). Everything the player reads about a special is these two words printed together ('Bomb Drop'): a step's lettering, the orders card's lines and the special's button. Identity, not tuning, so plain text.

id.about: The special's id, unique within the unit.

name.about: The name the player reads, capitalised ('Bomb').

action.about: The action the player reads after the name, capitalised ('Drop').
